original_question: If a polynomial M_p(T) with the properties in Question 9.3 exists, is it independent of the prime p, and is it equal to 8(g + 1)?
target_in_paper: Section 9, Question 9.5 (“Minimal maximal number of automorphisms of curves”), with notation from Definition 9.1 and the existence hypothesis imported from Question 9.3.
correct_elements: It correctly captures the conditional nature of the problem (“if the polynomial from Question 9.3 exists”) and the two follow-up issues asked in the paper’s Question 9.5: whether the polynomial is the same for different primes p, and whether it should be the characteristic-zero benchmark 8(g+1).
missing_details: The draft does not identify that its actual target is Question 9.5, not Question 9.3 itself.
It omits the definition of m(g; p): the maximum of #Aut(C) over all complete, irreducible, nonsingular algebraic curves C of genus g defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p.
It omits the genus range g >= 2 from Definition 9.1 and Question 9.3.
It omits that the polynomial sought in Question 9.3 lies in Q[T].
It omits the full hypothesis from Question 9.3: m(g; p) >= M_p(g) for every g >= 2, and m(g; p) = M_p(g) for infinitely many values of g.
It does not spell out that “independent of p” means: for any primes p and q, the corresponding polynomials are the same.
It uses 8(g+1) as though it were itself a polynomial in T; for a stand-alone formulation this should be stated as the polynomial 8(T+1).
It omits Remark 9.4, which states that if such a polynomial exists then it is unique; this explains why comparison across different primes is well-posed.
It does not indicate that 8(g+1) comes from the characteristic-zero comparison in Theorem 9.2(2).
refined_question: For a prime number p, let m(g; p) denote the maximum of #Aut(C) as C ranges over complete, irreducible, nonsingular algebraic curves of genus g >= 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p. Assume there exists a polynomial M_p(T) in Q[T] such that m(g; p) >= M_p(g) for every g >= 2 and m(g; p) = M_p(g) for infinitely many values of g. Must this polynomial be the same for all prime numbers p, and in fact equal to the polynomial 8(T+1)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s Question 9.5 in Section 9, because it repeats exactly the two questions asked there and refers back to the polynomial introduced in Question 9.3. To make it stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the notation m(g; p) from Definition 9.1, the precise existence hypothesis on M_p(T) from Question 9.3, and the uniqueness observation of Remark 9.4. Theorem 9.2 supplies the nearby characteristic-zero model explaining why 8(g+1) appears. The refined version therefore stays narrowly on the original intent of Question 9.5 while making all suppressed notation and quantifiers explicit.
